label: Room heater

questions.text: How many hours a day is the heater on?
questions.why: Long running heats parts and raises fire risk.

questions.text: Is it left on overnight or when nobody is in the room?
questions.why: Unattended heaters are a fire risk.

questions.text: Is it kept away from curtains, bedding and furniture?
questions.why: Things close to a heater can catch fire.

questions.text: Is it plugged into an extension board?
questions.why: Heaters draw a lot of power and can overheat extension boards.

questions.text: Are there small children or pets in the home?
Have you noticed a burning smell, sparks or the heater switching off by itself?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the heater before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: Cleaning an appliance that is plugged in risks an electric shock.

care_tips.text: Don't open the heater yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.

care_tips.text: Don't bypass or tamper with the thermostat or any safety cut-out.
care_tips.why: These stop the appliance overheating; without them it can cause burns or a fire.

care_tips.text: Switch the heater off when you leave the room or go to sleep.
Keep the heater well away from curtains, bedding and furniture.
care_tips.why: Fabric close to a heater can catch fire.

care_tips.text: Plug the heater straight into a wall socket of the right rating.
care_tips.why: Extension boards can overheat under the load.

care_tips.text: Keep children and pets away from the heater.
If you smell burning, see sparks or it keeps cutting out, unplug it and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: These can be signs of a dangerous fault.

reminders.text: Before winter, check the heater's cable and plug for damage (unplugged).
reminders.interval_text: about once a year, before winter
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
